note: Each beat is one action in the recording (record.mjs, by id) and what is said over it. `say` overrides `text` where the speech engine needs help; `text` is the caption. Short sentences: the captions show a few words at a time. `captions: false` marks a beat whose full-frame card already shows the words. Figures must match docs/numbers.md.

beats.text: Running a neural network on Ethereum costs almost two million gas. For one answer.
beats.say: Running a neural network on Ethereum costs almost two million gas. For one answer.

beats.text: So nobody runs it. Someone posts the answer, and stakes a bond on it. But what if it's a lie?
This is Tensile. It catches the lie by re-running a single neuron. And it's written in Fe.
beats.say: This is Tensile. It catches the lie by re-running a single neuron. And it's written in F E.

beats.text: Everything you'll see runs in this browser tab: a real Ethereum virtual machine, running exactly what the Fe compiler built.
beats.say: Everything you'll see runs in this browser tab: a real Ethereum virtual machine, running exactly what the F E compiler built.

beats.text: Let's draw a seven. The network runs the moment we let go: thirty-two hidden neurons, then ten outputs, all in integers.
The network says seven. Right, and computed fully on-chain. That's the expensive way.
Now let's lie, and claim it's a one. Not clumsily: we forge a few hidden neurons, then compute everything after them honestly. So the final answer looks consistent.
We post the lie, with one ether of play money as the bond.
A watcher re-runs the network off-chain, in WebAssembly, and finds the first neuron that doesn't match.
beats.say: A watcher re-runs the network off-chain, in web assembly, and finds the first neuron that doesn't match.

beats.text: Challenge only the final answer, and the contract refuses. The lie is hidden upstream.
So challenge the neuron itself. The contract checks the claim's hashes, proves the weights against the model's Merkle root, and re-runs that one neuron.
Slashed. Half the bond goes to the watcher, and half is burned. It cost under a tenth of the gas of running the whole network.
Now an honest claim, for contrast. We post the truth, and try to break it anyway. The contract refuses the challenge, with its own error. An hour later on the chain's clock, the claim is final.
Why Fe? Shapes and fixed-point scales live in the types. Wire up a layer of the wrong shape, and it doesn't compile.
beats.say: Why F E? Shapes and fixed-point scales live in the types. Wire up a layer of the wrong shape, and it doesn't compile.

beats.text: Effects are in the signatures, so only withdraw can send ether. And the safety is almost free: about two percent of a neuron's gas.

The NumPy reference and the native, WebAssembly and EVM builds agree on all ten thousand test images, bit for bit. We planted fifty-nine bugs in the contract. All fifty-nine were caught. And Fe costs 1.26 times the gas of a hand-written Solidity twin, per claim.
beats.say: The num pie reference and the native, web assembly and E V M builds agree on all ten thousand test images, bit for bit. We planted fifty-nine bugs in the contract. All fifty-nine were caught. And F E costs one point two six times the gas of a hand-written Solidity twin, per claim.

beats.text: And it's a tool, not one model. A generator writes the arbiter for any dense network. A second model, four times larger, costs four times the gas to run. And four percent more to dispute.
It's live on Sepolia. A dozen claims were posted there, and some are lies. Open the page, check them in your own browser, and slash one yourself.
beats.say: It's live on Seh-poh-lia. A dozen claims were posted there, and some are lies. Open the page, check them in your own browser, and slash one yourself.

beats.text: Tensile. A false answer, caught by one neuron.
